caption:
Most winter deaths in the UK aren't from hypothermia. They're heart attacks and strokes.

UKHSA says hypothermia directly causes about 50 deaths a year, while the cold's strain on the heart does far more harm. Health effects start when it's only 4 to 8°C outside, and indoors below 18°C.

You don't need 21°C everywhere. UKHSA's advice is at least 18°C in the rooms you use, and lots of thin layers instead of one thick one.
